unmapped_findings: 17Al alloy chemical composition (EDS, Table 1): Fe 43.2, Mn 34.8, Al 17.0, Cu 5.0 at.% (nominal Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu at.%).

Solution-treated (1100 °C/10 min + oil quench) baseline Vickers hardness of the 17Al alloy = 259.8 ± 1.5 HV (Table 3), i.e. belongs to the parent solution-treatment state rather than the 550 °C/10 h aged sample.

The peak hardness of the 17Al alloy (924.9 ± 25.8 HV) was reached by aging at 575 °C for 6 h, not by the 550 °C/10 h condition; the hardest 17Al sample's intrinsic β-Mn hardness measured by nanoindentation was 12.2 ± 0.1 GPa (average nanoindentation hardness of that sample = 11.1 ± 0.6 GPa).

For the hardest 17Al sample (575 °C/6 h, 924.9 HV), the indentation-measured fracture toughness KIC was 6.6 MPa·m^1/2 (average crack length 22 µm, elastic modulus 175 GPa); these are not values of the 550 °C/10 h sample.
β-Mn micro-area composition in the hardest 17Al sample (SEM-EDS, Fig. 14): Mn 36.2, Al 16.3, Cu 2.6 at.% (measured on the 575 °C/6 h sample, not the 550 °C/10 h sample).

The volume fraction of FCC Cu-rich + BCC precipitates in the 17Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 10 h was 4.7 % with an average Vickers hardness of 833.2 HV (a different aging condition from the 550 °C/10 h sample).
Proposed general aging phase-evolution sequence for the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu steels: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase.
